title: Saying sorry
subtitle: Pedir perdón
review: Written by Claude in Latin American (Mexican) Spanish. Check the Spanish, the English and the notes before recording audio. English support only.

categories.desc: A quick sorry, a real apology, and owning up.
cards: The quick everyday sorry: you bump into someone, you interrupt.
Stronger: for bad news or real regret. Lo siento mucho: I'm very sorry.
Lo siento mucho. No puedo ir a tu fiesta.
I'm very sorry. I can't come to your party.
Disculpa la tardanza. Había mucho tráfico.
Sorry I'm late. There was a lot of traffic.
Perdón, rompí el vaso. Fue sin querer.
Sorry, I broke the glass. I didn't mean to.
About something already done: fue mi culpa.
Perdón, es mi culpa. Olvidé las llaves.
Sorry, it's my fault. I forgot the keys.

categories.desc: Getting someone's attention, and getting past.
cards: To get a stranger's attention politely, with usted.
Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
To pass someone, or to leave a table or a room. The answer: pase.
Perdón por llegar tarde. Se me hizo tarde.
Sorry I'm late. I lost track of time.
Polite, with usted: before taking a chair or reaching past someone.

categories.desc: What to answer when someone says sorry.
cards: — Perdón, llegué tarde. — No pasa nada.
— Lo siento, olvidé tu libro. — No te preocupes.
— I'm sorry, I forgot your book. — Don't worry.
— ¿Puedo llegar a las seis? — No hay problema.
— Can I come at six? — No problem.
Calm acceptance. Said with a sigh, it means 'fine, if you say so'.
— Perdón por el ruido. — Está bien.
— Sorry about the noise. — It's OK.
